hypothesis: The bridge-equation nowcast of quarterly real GDP growth (q/q), made 30 days after the quarter ends from the monthly activity index and/or OECD leading indicator published by then, has a lower RMSE than the historical mean of GDP growth published by then.
knownLimits: Release lags are fixed rules (GDP 60 days, activity 45, leading indicator 45), not each country's actual calendar.
Values are today's vintage (later revisions included); no real-time data vintages are free for all countries, so this is a pseudo real-time test.
Countries with no monthly indicator are left out; quarters where no indicator month was out are left out (the fallback AR is not what is being tested).
OECD leading indicator via DBnomics lags about five months today; the test uses the OECD's own lag, so it measures the method, not today's mirror delay.
Not compared with past IMF WEO forecasts: the app holds only today's WEO vintage, so an IMF benchmark cannot be scored without look-ahead. A later version can add it once past vintages are stored.
